speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What two kinds of indirect initiation?
premises: Now indirect initiation is twofold: the dead one, and the jīva-part.
inference: Parokṣa-dīkṣā splits into mṛta and jīvaṃśa — the chapter's two subjects.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Who is commanded to be initiated thus?
premises: One who has served the guru — dead, banished, sorcery-killed, infant-killed, arisen at the death-moment, or power-descent through another mouth — likewise one to be initiated: such the command.
inference: The ājñā lists the eligible cases: guru-service plus the death-circumstances, closed by the catch-all 'to be initiated'.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Is adhivāsa used for the dead?
premises: And in the dead-initiation, adhivāsa-and-rest is not used.
inference: Mṛtadīkṣā excludes adhivāsa-ādi — the living-rite preliminaries dropped.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What are the presence-causes in the mandala?
premises: In the mandala: abundant rite, supreme instrument, flower-and-rest seat, pedestal-and-rest, trident-lotus form, specific meditation-mantra, itself radiant — of the meditation-devoted yogi, the one-devotion-immersion-rich, and the knower: these are the saṃnidhāna-hetavaḥ, stated in order.
inference: Seven presence-causes (kriyā, upakaraṇa, sthāna, maṇḍala, ākṛti, dhyeya-mantra, radiant self) plus the two yogic subjects — the sequence is authoritative.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What happens when they come together?
premises: In their conjunction, what talk would there be? — thus it was said by the Supreme Lord.
inference: Samuditatve makes the question rhetorical: once present, nothing further to ask — divine verdict.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What does the seer do after worship?
premises: Having worshipped the god and established his form, by the guru-derived teaching-order let him see it; rising from muladhara, crossing by seminal power the endless nerve-path-staff to the nose-sky — let him seek to pervade.
inference: The jāla-sequence: worship → establish → see by guru-order → muladhara-rise → nāḍī-crossing to nāsāgagana → vyāpti-desire.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: How long does the great jala-named practice run?
premises: As long as, by smoke heaped fine-flame mesh, the path-wheel is covered and the desired jīva is brought — thus the great jala-named practice.
inference: The practice's duration = smoke-coverage of dhvacakra + ānayana of the jīva — named mahā-jalānāma-prayoga.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What does the covering achieve?
premises: By this, the to-be-covered goes into another's power — facing first; afterwards the whole is brought, if — or then even from the path's middle, as he wishes.
inference: Acchādanīya enters paravaśa (saṃmukhīnatvam ādau); the whole follows paścāt or adhvamadhyāt yatheṣṭam.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Which yoga is this, told by whom?
premises: Two-drawn or two-raised, or in a dead person's scope: the yoga gone through blessed Śaṃbhunātha's tradition — jala-named, told by me.
inference: The ākṛṣṭāv/uddhatau/mṛtajana scopes are covered by the jālanāmā yoga as transmitted by Śrīśaṃbhunātha-āgama and authored here.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Why does the outside case not behave the same?
premises: Outside too — how does it not happen? From drawing-and-rest without practice, if asked: by passion-hatred-yoga-vaśa in its operation, from the aiśvarya-āveśa-yoga.
inference: The outside fails without abhyāsa — its operation runs on rāga-dveṣa-yoga-vaśa, not on the aiśvarya-immersion that inner drawing has.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What follows from niyati-niyantrita?
premises: Then, from being necessarily controlled, dependence on practice-and-rest would indeed be.
inference: Because the krama is niyata-niyamtrita, abhyāsa-āpekṣā follows necessarily.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What differs here?
premises: Here, however, from immersion in grace-natured Lordhood, such is the state.
inference: Iha-tu: the grace-natured parameśvara-tāveśa produces tathābhāva directly — no practice-dependence.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Who does the gracing, and by what door?
premises: For the Supreme Lord himself, by the door of the guru's body-abode, graces those to be graced.
inference: Anugraha flows parameśvara → guru-śarīra-adhiṣṭhāna-dvāra → anugrāhyāḥ.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What is said of him?
premises: And he, of unthinkable glory — it is mostly said.
inference: Acintya-mahimā: the claim is ukta-prāyam — mostly told, hedge kept.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What becomes of the drawn jīva, and does he tremble?
premises: Thus drawn by jala-practice, the jīva enters dārbha, jasmine-fruit or body, becomes; nor trembles — equipment absent; but by that contemplation's force trembles even so: purification-consecration, within the full-offering's yojana-end.
inference: Entered-body samāviṣṭa has no spanda (sāmagrī-absence) yet has tadanudhyāna-bala spanda — the double movement ends in prokṣaṇa-saṃskāra within pūrṇāhuti-yojanā.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What happens to the dārbha-form in the fire?
premises: Here, further, by the full-offering, dissolution of the dārbha-and-rest form in the supreme fire is to be done.
inference: Pūrṇāhuti effects laya of the dārbhādyākāra in paratejas.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: When is the raised one released?
premises: Thus raised out, he is released by the full-offering itself — if he stands in hell-ghost-animal classes.
inference: Apavāra by pūrṇāhutyā eva, conditioned on the svarnāraka-preta-tiryak standing.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What does a man obtain then?
premises: A man, just then, obtains knowledge, yoga, initiation, or discernment.
inference: Manuṣya-tadaiva: jñāna/yoga/dīkṣā/viveka available in the same moment.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Why can the dead be raised?
premises: From being an eligible body — thus the raising-of-the-dead.
inference: Adhikāri-śarīratva grounds mṛtoddharaṇa — eligibility, not sentiment.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What is the krama for the living too?
premises: Even for the living, in indirect initiation when power-descent arises: this very sequence — excepting dārbha-form-imagination jīva-drawing.
inference: The same krama extends to jīvataḥ parokṣa-utpanna-śaktipāta, minus the dārbha-ākṛti-kalpana-ākṛṣṭi.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Who gets consecrated without the rite?
premises: The consecration of the one established by mere meditation itself.
inference: Dhyāna-mātra-upasthāpita alone suffices for saṃskāra — meditation-established, no fire.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What does dīkṣā give?
premises: Initiation gives both the enjoyment and the enjoyer.
inference: Bhoga-bhokṣa-ubhaya-dāyinī — dīkṣā grants both sides of enjoyment at once.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Why is the higher-doctrine consecration stronger for many?
premises: From the strength of one's own habit, and the unthinkability of severing the enjoyment-habit: by many, in initiation, the higher-doctrine consecration is strong; another would be for that consecration.
inference: Sva-vāsanā-balīyastva + bhoga-vāsanā-viccheda-asambhāvyamānatva make ūrdhva-śāsana-saṃskāra balavān for the many; anya is for that saṃskāra.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What of the initiated from outside?
premises: Likewise for the initiated from outside — the manifestation of knowledge-and-rest, it is said.
inference: Paroṣa-dīkṣita gets jñāna-ādy-āvirbhāva tathaiva — the same outward-benefit clause extends.
